slices.name: R1 non-silent sync: surface sync_to_proposals() failures in the agent prompt
slices.goal:
sync_to_proposals() records per-SHA outcomes and the wrapper prepends
a NOT-synced banner to the fetched event prompt on any failure;
the event-prompt empty-delta caution cross-references the banner.
Sync behavior itself is unchanged.

tasks.description:
Record per-SHA sync outcomes and prepend the failure banner. In
`orchestrator/consensus_wrapper.py` `sync_to_proposals()`
(≈487-541), record an outcome per proposal SHA — `merged`,
`already-ancestor`, `unresolvable`, `merge-failed` — at each
currently fail-soft step (unresolvable SHA ≈524-526; failed or
conflicting merge ≈534-535). On any failure outcome, the wrapper
prepends a banner to the fetched event prompt BEFORE invoking the
agent: "worktree NOT synced to `<sha>` (`<reason>`); treat your
local diff as unreliable — use the `git show` commands below."
Keep the existing log lines; sync/abort semantics are unchanged —
only outcome recording and banner prepending are new.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
- A conflicting merge yields a `merge-failed` outcome and the
  banner (with SHA and reason) in the prompt handed to the agent.
- An unresolvable SHA yields `unresolvable` + banner.
- `merged` and `already-ancestor` outcomes produce no banner and a
  byte-identical prompt.
- Merge/abort behavior of sync_to_proposals() is unchanged.

tasks.description:
Cross-reference the banner from the empty-delta caution. Update the
empty-delta caution text in
`orchestrator/routes/event_prompt.py` (≈266-281, inside
`_render_producer_delta_section`) to point at the wrapper banner:
when the delta is empty AND the worktree may not be synced, the
caution tells the reviewer to check for the NOT-synced banner and
fall back to the rendered `git show` commands. No other rendering
changes in this slice.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
- Empty-delta caution names the NOT-synced banner and the
  `git show` fallback.
- Non-empty-delta rendering is byte-identical to today.

tasks.description:

tasks.acceptance_criteria:

slices.name: Gateway artifact-read endpoint (strict, name-resolving) + sandbox helper
slices.goal:
POST /api/v1/artifact/get serves committed artifact content by
spec-registered name + hex-validated ref via git show on the
authoritative repo (gateway blueprint forwarding to a new orchestrator
route), with a sandbox-side helper. Unblocks #3002.

tasks.description:
Orchestrator artifact-read route: add
`orchestrator/routes/artifacts.py` (NEW), registered per the
existing `orchestrator/routes/` convention. Request: artifact
`name` (spec-registered), `ref` (hex-validated commit SHA), and
the issue/pipeline identifier. Resolves the path via
`artifact_spec.resolve_artifact_path` and returns the content of
`git show <ref>:<path>` from the authoritative repo, applying the
existing output caps with a `truncated` flag. STRICT per HITL Q2:
the schema has NO path field; an unregistered name returns 400
listing registered names; a non-hex ref returns 400; an
unresolvable ref or path-absent-at-ref returns a structured 4xx,
never a 500. Cross-link #3002 in the module docstring.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
- Registered name + valid ref returns committed content
  byte-identical to the blob; oversized content is capped with
  `truncated: true`.
- Unregistered name → 400 listing registered names; non-hex ref
  → 400; absent-at-ref → structured 4xx.
- No request field accepts a repo path (schema-level).
- Works with no shared object store between agent worktree and
  orchestrator repo (server-side git show only).

decisions.question: Scope for issue #3077 pipeline: phase 1 already landed (PR #3078/#3083). Which remaining scope should this pipeline deliver? Option A = phase-1 residual (non-silent sync_to_proposals) + ratchet only; Option B = residual + phase 2 (artifact spec, spec-derived propose validation, gateway artifact-read endpoint unblocking #3002); Option C (recommended) = B + phase 3 cleanup (delete REVIEWER-SYNC fetch prose, docs invariant, no-sync-mechanics-in-prompts ratchet test) + bounded durability (fail-loud when BRC runs on the in-memory message-store backend). See .egg-state/drafts/issue-3077-analysis.md "Scope Options".

Durability bar for the BRC message store (clause-1 prerequisite, issue #3077): is a fail-loud signal sufficient when EGG_MESSAGE_STORE_BACKEND resolves to the in-memory backend while BRC phases run (recommended — bounded), or should 'auto' refuse to run BRC phases without Redis Streams (stricter, but breaks dev setups without Redis)?

options.label: Fail-loud warning/health signal on memory backend (recommended)
Refuse to run BRC phases without Redis
Defer durability entirely to the #3070 lineage

decisions.question: [Phase gate: refine] The refine phase has completed. Please review the analysis and approve to continue, or provide feedback to request changes.
decisions.resolution:
## Resolved Questions

**Q1 — Scope (Option A / B / C):** Option C — full remaining scope: R1 non-silent sync residual + artifact spec module + spec-derived propose validation for all producers + gateway artifact-read endpoint (strict) + Phase-3 prose cleanup, docs/architecture invariant entry, and ratchet test + bounded durability.

**Q2 — Endpoint resolution surface:** Strict — the gateway artifact-read endpoint accepts only spec-registered artifact names (no raw repo-path escape hatch). Path-guessing is the disease this issue retires; keep the gateway policy surface small.

**Q3 — Durability bar:** Fail-loud is sufficient for this pipeline — a prominent startup warning/health signal when BRC consensus runs on the in-memory message-store backend, plus a restart-semantics test for the Redis Streams path (distinguishing the designed _clear_concurrent_state() phase-boundary wipe from accidental mid-phase restart loss). Do NOT change `auto` to refuse BRC without Redis; deeper durability work stays in the #3070 lineage.

pr.title: Serve coordination state: artifact spec + gateway reads (#3077)
pr.description:
Issue #3077 identifies a recurring failure class: pipeline coordination
state has one logical home but N physical replicas (orchestrator/gateway/
per-agent worktrees, origin, per-role branches), synchronized by ad-hoc git
choreography and prompt prose. Eleven-plus incidents trace to this; served
channels (contract API, consensus signals) have produced zero. Phase 1
(PRs #3078/#3083) landed served BRC transcript reads and wrapper-performed
sync. This change lands the HITL-approved remaining scope (Option C) on
the architect's six-slice DAG (slices 1-5 serialized, slice 6 parallel):

1. **R1 non-silent sync.** `sync_to_proposals()` records per-SHA outcomes
   and the wrapper prepends a "worktree NOT synced" banner to the fetched
   event prompt on any failure, so a reviewer whose worktree silently
   failed to sync can no longer trust a stale local diff.
2. **Artifact spec.** A declarative registry
   (`shared/egg_contracts/artifact_spec.py`) becomes the single source of
   truth for artifact name → path template → phase → producer → consumers,
   with mandatory consistency tests pinning every existing hardcoding
   (gateway phase gates, `_get_draft_path`, prompt literals) to it.
3. **Spec-derived validation.** Propose-time draft validation generalizes
   from plan-only to every refine/plan producer with a registered
   artifact, subsuming `_validate_producer_draft_present` and reusing the
   #3081 graceful-degradation git-show helper; plan keeps its parseability
   and role-alignment extensions.
4. **Gateway artifact reads.** `POST /api/v1/artifact/get` serves
   committed artifact content by spec-registered name + hex-validated ref
   via `git show` against the authoritative repo — strict, no raw-path
   escape hatch (HITL) — removing the shared-object-store assumption and
   unblocking #3002. A sandbox `egg-artifact` helper gives agents one
   verb.
5. **Prose retirement + ratchet.** REVIEWER-SYNC fetch prose and the
   event-prompt self-fetch fallback are deleted now that served reads
   cover them; `docs/architecture` gains the three-clause invariant entry;
   a ratchet test keeps sync mechanics out of agent-facing prompts.
6. **Bounded durability.** `auto`→memory fallback fails loud (error log +
   degraded health flag; explicit memory stays a warning) and a Redis
   restart-semantics test distinguishes accidental mid-phase loss from the
   designed `_clear_concurrent_state()` phase-boundary wipe. Per HITL,
   `auto` selection semantics are unchanged; deeper work stays in #3070.
